lean.statement: ∀ {d n : ℕ}, 3 ≤ n → n ≤ d → ∀ {κ : ℝ}, 4 ≤ κ → ∀ (O : Fin (d / n) → Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ), let A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ := (let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d := ((Equiv.sumCongr ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv) (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n)); Matrix.reindex e e (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun j => ((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + (O j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose))) 0 0 (1 : Matrix (Fin (d % n)) (Fin (d % n)) ℝ))); let f : (Fin d → ℝ) → ℝ := fun x => (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (x ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ x)); f 0 = 0 ∧ ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x ∧ (f x = 0 ↔ x = 0)
approved_definition_context: The displayed anonymous term expands the matrix definition and its finite-coordinate equivalence; no source or theorem identity is provided.

Matrix.blockDiagonal indexes pairs as (inner coordinate, block). prodComm before finProdFinEquiv places the blocks consecutively; the tail starts at (d/n)*n. Matrix.reindex uses inverse coordinate maps.
Fin0 is the empty type, so its identity matrix has no coordinates. The remainder d%n equals d-(d/n)*n.
Over ℝ, IsHermitian means symmetric. dotProduct is the sum of coordinate products, giving squared Euclidean norm when both vectors agree; mulVec is ordinary matrix-vector multiplication.
